Boeing Digital Services

Amplitude Bake Off Guide

Use cases and workflows

November 2026
IntroSet up1 Workflow2 Adoption3 Segments4 Flags5 Guides6 Problems7 Accounts8 ExportsWrap upBonus

Eight scenarios cover 23 of the 26 use cases and 12 of the 14 workflows in Boeing's packet. Start with Set up your workspace: you will create a folder in your own Space and save your work there, then gather it all into one dashboard at the end. Each scenario gives the question, numbered steps, and what you should see. The rest (CPUC-16, 17, 18 and CPWF-10, 11) need admin access and are not part of this hands-on guide.

About the data

Everything in this sandbox is synthetic dummy data. Conversion rates, user counts, error volumes, and other numbers will not look the way they would in a real Boeing scenario, so please don't be concerned if a percentage or total seems unusual. The sandbox shows how Amplitude answers your questions, not what your own numbers would say.

How to read a scenario

Steps are numbered. Menu paths are in bold, for example Create > Chart > Funnel tab.
ID tags such as CPUC-01 show which of Boeing's use cases or workflows a step answers.
Screenshots sit beside the step they show and say which step they belong to. Click any screenshot to expand it.

The sandbox

Sample portal: open https://amplitude-boeingdigital-demo.lovable.app, sign in with any username and any password (for example guide.tester / test1234), and choose a product: Airplane Health Management, Toolbox, or Asset Lifecycle Planning. Your activity appears in Amplitude within a few minutes.

Amplitude: sign in to the boeing-digital-amplitude organization. The Boeing Digital Portfolio View combines all three products; each product also has its own project. To open it, click the project dropdown in the top-left navigation (next to the organization name) and select Boeing Digital Portfolio View from the cross-project views list. Four dashboards are pinned and ready in the Portfolio view: Daily watchlist · Operator account review · Operator health · Executive summary. Cohorts, flags, guides, and surveys are ready for you to use.

Terms used in this guide

TermMeaning
OperatorAn airline customer. company_code (a user property) is the operator's short code, for example SKP for SkyPath Airlines or TRA for TransArc.
CohortA saved group of users defined by what they did. Build one with Create > Cohort and use it as a filter on any chart.
Fault Finder adopterPerformed Fault Finder Used at least 1 time in the last 30 days. A non-adopter was active in the last 30 days but is not part of the adopters cohort.
Frequent / light userFrequent: Fault Finder Used at least 3 times in the last 30 days. Light: 1 or 2 times in the last 30 days.
Lapsed userPerformed Fault Finder Used at least once in the last 60 days and is not part of the Fault Finder adopters cohort.
Errors, no usePerformed Error Occurred at least once in the last 30 days and is not part of the Fault Finder adopters cohort.
MicroscopeClick a data point or bar on a chart to see the users behind it. From there: create a cohort, view users, watch session replays, or run Root Cause Analysis.
User vs event propertyA User Property describes the person (for example company_code, user_role). An Event Property describes one event (for example error_type).
Housekeeping

This sandbox is shared by about 30 testers. Put your initials before the name of anything you save, in the format [Initials] - Name, for example [EB] - New user cohort, and save it in your own folder (see Set up your workspace). Preview guides and surveys instead of publishing them. Do not activate flags or start experiments, and do not connect any destination or source or send data into or out of Amplitude.

Get started

Set up your workspace

Where will you save your work, and how will you find it again?

Where to start

Click All Content & Spaces in the left sidebar.

1.Click All Content & Spaces in the left sidebar, then click My Space in the list on the left. This is your personal Space, named after you. Only you have access to it, so it is a safe place to save your work.

2.Click the + sign on the left-hand side to add a new folder, name it [Initials] - Bake Off (for example [EB] - Bake Off), and click Create. Your folder appears under Folders on the left.

3.From now on, save every chart, cohort, and other item you build with your initials first, in the format [Initials] - Name, for example [EB] - Fault Finder adopters. When the Save window opens, type the name, open the Location dropdown, choose your own Space and then your folder, click Move, and click Save.

What you should see

A folder in your own Space where everything you save in this guide lives, ready to gather into a dashboard at the end.

Scenario 1

Follow users through a workflow

Where do users drop off, loop, or get stuck, and does it differ by operator?

Where to start

Start in the Boeing Digital Portfolio View (see The sandbox above).

1.Select Create > Chart, then open the Funnel tab. In the Events module add Event Detail Viewed, then Alert Status Changed, then Task Card Created. The date range control at the top right of the chart shows Last 30 days, which is the range this guide uses.CPUC-01

2.Below the events, under Group Segment by, click Select property..., search for company_code, and choose the one with the person icon (the user property).CPUC-01

3.Read the result. The bars show conversion at each step for every operator, and the table below the chart shows conversion and time to convert. In the sandbox data, the biggest drop is between Alert Status Changed and Task Card Created. Click Save, name the chart [Initials] - Alert to task card funnel, and save it to your folder.CPUC-03

4.First remove the company_code grouping under Group Segment by so the funnel shows all users together as a single bar. Do not save over your saved chart. Then click the striped bar in the Task Card Created column, which represents the users who dropped off. In the menu that opens (the Microscope), choose Create Cohort, name it [Initials] - Alert triage drop-offs, and save it to your folder.CPUC-01

5.Select Create > Chart and open the Journeys tab. Change starting with to ending with and add Task Card Created. The Pathfinder shows the step that came right before it. Click More at the left of Step 1 to reveal one more earlier step, and click it again until you see three steps. Then click an event name above a column, for example Document Bookmarked, and choose Create Funnel to turn that route into a funnel. Save the Journeys chart as [Initials] - Path to task card.CPUC-01CPUC-02

6.Click Sessions & Zoning in the left sidebar, then Session Replay, and open the All Replays tab. Click + Filter, choose Event, search for Rage Click, and select [Amplitude] Rage Click. To see only the drop-off users, click + Filter again, choose Cohort, and pick your [Initials] - Alert triage drop-offs cohort. Click a replay to play it.CPUC-02

7.For search to action, switch to the Toolbox project with the project dropdown at the top of the chart screen, and repeat step 1 with Search Submitted, Document Opened, and Task Card Created.CPWF-01

What you should see

A funnel with a clear drop, different conversion by operator, a cohort of drop-off users, a path that leads to a task card, and a replay of a frustrating moment.

Scenario 2

Adoption, retention, and engagement

Is a new feature being adopted, do users come back, and why does engagement move?

Where to start

Start in the Toolbox project. Use the project dropdown at the top of the chart screen to switch.

1.Select Create > Chart, open the Segmentation tab, and add the event Fault Finder Used. At the top right of the chart, set the date range to Last 90 days, then open the interval dropdown next to it (it says Daily) and choose Weekly. Under Group Segment by, choose User Property > user_role. Save the chart as [Initials] - Fault Finder adoption by role.CPUC-04

2.Select Create > Cohort. Next to The Users who, click select condition, choose performed event, then click Select event... and choose Fault Finder Used. Leave count >= 1 and Last 30 days, and save it as [Initials] - Fault Finder adopters. For a second cohort, choose performed event with Any Active Event (count >= 1, Last 30 days), click + Add > cohort, change part to not part, choose your adopters cohort, and save it as [Initials] - Fault Finder non-adopters. Amplitude cannot select users with zero events, so non-adopters are built by excluding the adopters. If you can already see cohorts called Fault Finder adopters and Fault Finder non-adopters in Amplitude, you can use those as an alternative.CPUC-04

3.Select Create > Chart and open the Retention tab. Change the starting event from New Users to Any Active Event, keep Any Active Event as the return event, and choose Return On or After. Under Segment by, click + In Cohort on segment 1, tick your adopters cohort, and click Apply. Click + Add Segment, click + In Cohort on segment 2, and apply your non-adopters cohort. Compare the two lines, then save the chart as [Initials] - Fault Finder retention.CPUC-05CPWF-02

4.Select Create > Chart, open the Segmentation tab, choose Any Event, and measure unique users. Set the interval to Weekly and the date range to Last 90 days. Above the chart, click Chart Settings, choose Anomalies & Forecast, and click Enable Anomaly & Forecast. The chart shows an expected range around the line, and points outside it are anomalies. Click an unusual point to open the Microscope and choose Analyze Root Cause, then open the Root Cause Analysis tab below the chart.CPUC-06

What you should see

Weekly adoption since release, retention for users and non-users of the feature, and an explanation of what drove a change. If no anomalies appear, try a different event (for example Error Occurred) or add a Group by (for example company_code or error_type).

Scenario 3

Segments and identity

Who behaves alike, and is each person recognized across products?

Where to start

Start in the Toolbox project.

1.CPUC-13CPUC-11

These four cohorts are used in this guide. Look in All Content & Spaces first: if you can already see them, use them as they are and skip the rest of this step.

To build your own, select Create > Cohort. Each condition reads did perform [event], with count [operator] [number], during [time range]. Click + Add for a second condition, and change part to not part to exclude another cohort. Name each cohort with your initials, for example [Initials] - Light users.

  1. Frequent users
    • Fault Finder Used, count >= 3, during the Last 30 days
  2. Light users
    • Fault Finder Used, count >= 1, during the Last 30 days
    • + Add: Fault Finder Used, count <= 2, during the Last 30 days
  3. Lapsed users
    • Fault Finder Used, count >= 1, during the Last 60 days
    • + Add: not part of the Fault Finder adopters cohort
  4. Errors, no use
    • Error Occurred, count >= 1, during the Last 30 days
    • + Add: not part of the Fault Finder adopters cohort

2.Click Events & Users in the left sidebar, then User Profiles. The page lists recently active users. Click the blue Amplitude ID of any user to open that person's profile; you can pick any user. Scroll the left panel to see the user properties. The Activity tab shows the event stream, which lists everything that user did (events from all three products when you start in the Portfolio view). Click one event in the stream, then scroll the left panel to the Groups section, which shows the company (operator) the user belongs to.CPUC-14CPWF-05

What you should see

Named user segments, one identity across products, and the operator each user belongs to.

Scenario 4

Feature flags and experiments

Can we release a feature to a chosen group, and test a change?

Where to start

Click Experiment in the left sidebar (not the Experiments tab inside a user profile), and use the Toolbox project.

1.Click Experiment in the left sidebar, then Feature Flags, and open toolbox-quick-bookmarks. Look, but do not change anything. Audience Targeting decides who can get the feature (audience, a rollout percentage, and segments you add). Variants lists what users can receive. Activate flag switches the flag on for the real website, so do not click it: about 30 people share this sandbox, and changing this flag would change the portal for all of them.CPUC-15

2.To practice, build your own flag. Select Create > Feature Flag, type a name such as [Initials] - Quick bookmarks test, check that the project says Toolbox, and click Create. On the flag page, under Audience Targeting, click + Add Segment, add the user property company_code equal to SKP, and set the Rollout to 50%. Do not click Activate flag.CPUC-15

3.Scroll to the Testing section of your flag. It lets you list specific User IDs or cohorts that should receive the on or off variant, which is how a team checks a rollout on their own account before activating it for everyone. You do not need to fill it in.CPUC-15

4.Click Experiment > Experiments and open [Sample] Toolbox Search Suggestions. It shows what a finished setup looks like: the hypothesis, Metrics (a primary metric and secondary metrics), Variants (Control and Suggested tools), Audience Targeting, and Delivery. Do not start it.CPUC-25CPWF-12

5.To see how you would set up your own, select Create > Experiment. The menu offers two choices: Web (full-page web changes) and Feature (changes inside the product). Stop there, or open the setup and stop before you click Start Experiment.CPUC-25CPWF-12

6.Select Create > Chart, open 10 more, and choose Experiment Results. This chart compares variants on a metric once an experiment has data: add the metric under Metrics, the exposure event under Exposure, and read the variants against the control. There is no running experiment in the sandbox, so it stays empty. This is where results appear.CPUC-25CPWF-12

What you should see

How a flag decides who gets a feature, how an experiment is set up around a flag, and where results appear. Nothing is switched on in the sandbox, so there is no live data.

Scenario 5

Guides and surveys

Can we guide users, ask how it went, and see how it performed?

Where to start

Click Guides & Surveys in the left sidebar, and use the Toolbox project.

1.Select Create > Guide. In the window, click Start a blank guide instead of choosing a template.CPUC-26CPWF-04

2.Build and test a Pin guide in the builder:CPUC-12CPUC-11CPWF-04

  1. Click the step type dropdown at the top of step 1 (it may show Modal, Popover, or Pin) and select Pin, which attaches the step to an element on a page.
  2. Set the title to Search by fault code or manual title.
  3. Add a button. You can keep the text Done or change it.
  4. Save the guide with the title [Initials] - Sample Guide.
  5. Click Select Target and enter the URL https://amplitude-boeingdigital-demo.lovable.app/toolbox/library (the portal's Toolbox Library page).
  6. Select the search bar on the page and click Save.
  7. Click Preview to see how your guide looks to users. Do not publish the guide.
  8. Open the Setup tab. Under Targeting, you can select one of the cohorts you created in the earlier steps, for example [Initials] - Light users.

3.Build and test a survey. Select Create > Survey and choose to start blank instead of using a template, then in the builder:CPUC-22

  1. Select Popover as the step type.
  2. Set the title to How easy was it to create a task card?
  3. Add a block and choose Stars (or any rating you prefer).
  4. Add two buttons: Submit and Remind me later.
  5. Save the survey with the title [Initials] - Sample survey.
  6. Click Preview and enter the URL https://amplitude-boeingdigital-demo.lovable.app/toolbox/tasks (the portal's Toolbox tasks page) to see how your survey looks to users. Do not publish the survey.
  7. Open the Setup tab. Under Targeting, you can select one of the cohorts you created in the earlier steps.

4.Click Surveys and open [Sample] Toolbox Ease-of-Use Survey, then click its Insights and Responses tabs. This is where you see how a survey performs: views, completions, and each answer. Because this is a demo instance and the survey may not be collecting responses, there may be little or no data to see.CPUC-26CPUC-22CPWF-04

What you should see

A guide and a survey set up without code, previews of how users see them, and the places where engagement and responses appear once a survey is live. To see finished examples, click Guides & Surveys, then Guides, and open [Sample] Getting Started with Toolbox: the steps are on the left and a live preview is on the right. Go back, click Surveys, and open [Sample] Toolbox Ease-of-Use Survey and the survey named survey to see finished surveys.

Scenario 6

Problems, alerts, and AI insights

Who is hit by errors, who should be told, and can Amplitude explain what happened?

Where to start

Start in the Boeing Digital Portfolio View (see The sandbox above).

1.Select Create > Chart, open the Segmentation tab, and add Error Occurred. Click + Group-by under the event and choose the event property error_type. Under Group Segment by, choose the user property company_code. At the top right of the chart, set the date range to Last 14 days. This is a line chart. Save it as [Initials] - Errors by type and operator.CPUC-09

2.Hover over the highest point on the line and click the + that appears to open the Microscope. Choose View Users to see who is behind it. To watch a session, choose Watch Session Replays. Replays exist only for recent live sessions, so if the Microscope says no replays match, open Session Replay > All Replays, add the filter Event is Error Occurred, and play one.CPUC-09CPWF-09

3.Select Create > Chart and open the Funnel tab. Add Error Occurred as the first event and Task Card Created as the second. You do not need to filter anything; to compare operators, add company_code under Group Segment by. The chart shows how many users who hit an error went on to create a task card. Saving it is optional: save it as [Initials] - Error to task card if you want it on your final dashboard.CPWF-03

4.Click All Content & Spaces in the left sidebar, open the Amplitude + Boeing Shared Content space (under Joined Spaces), and open the Daily watchlist dashboard. Look at the Errors by operator chart at the bottom. Find the highest point on any line, hover over it, and click the + to open the Microscope. Choose View Users to see the users behind that spike.CPUC-08CPWF-08

5.A dashboard agent watches a dashboard for you. On the Daily watchlist dashboard, click Monitor at the top right, then Create New Agent. The Dashboard Agent page asks for the dashboard to watch, an agent name (use [Initials] - Daily watchlist agent), a short description of what to monitor (for example, 'Tell me when errors rise for any operator'), and where to send updates (email, Slack, or Teams) and how often. Review the settings. Do not connect Slack or Teams, and stop before you click Create unless you want email updates.CPUC-08CPUC-23

6.Open a saved chart, such as Errors by operator from the dashboard, and click the bell icon. Choose Set Up Alert. Keep the default criteria (outside the range of a 99% confidence interval) or add a condition, and look at the Notifications options (email, Slack, and Teams). Do not connect Slack or Teams. Click Cancel unless you want to save the alert.CPUC-08CPUC-10

What you should see

The error types and operators affected, a replay of a failing session, a dashboard agent and an alert that tell you when something changes.

Scenario 7

Accounts and health

How is one operator doing against its peers, and can we score health?

Where to start

Start in the Amplitude + Boeing Shared Content space (All Content & Spaces, under Joined Spaces).

1.Open the saved Operator account review dashboard. Its charts cover the last 60 days; to change the range, use the date control in the filter bar. Click Add Filter at the top, search for company_code, and choose the one with the person icon (the user property). Pick one operator, for example TRA or SKP, and click Apply.CPUC-07CPWF-07

2.To compare the operator with the others, remove the company_code filter you just added (click the x on it), then click the title of the Active users by operator chart to open it. It is already grouped by company_code, so each line is one operator. Hover over the lines to compare them.CPUC-07

3.Go back to the dashboard, click Analyze at the top right, and ask: What changed for operator TRA in the last 30 days? The Global Agent can take a little while to build its answer, so you may need to be patient while you wait for the output.CPUC-07CPWF-07

4.Open the saved Operator health dashboard, which is also in the Amplitude + Boeing Shared Content space (All Content & Spaces, under Joined Spaces). Each chart is one signal: active users, task card users, Fault Finder users, and errors. The Operator health score chart combines them with a formula.CPUC-21CPWF-13

5.Click the title of the Operator health score chart to open it, change one weight in the formula, and watch the line move. Do not save over the original chart.CPUC-21CPWF-13

What you should see

A one-page picture of an operator, a comparison with the other operators, and a configurable health score.

Scenario 8

Reports, exports, and integrations

How can we share dashboards, export raw data, use Power BI, and sync to other systems?

Where to start

Open the Executive summary dashboard in All Content & Spaces (Amplitude + Boeing Shared Content). This section is for looking only: do not connect a destination or source, and do not send data into or out of Amplitude.

Optional

This scenario is optional. It has few hands-on steps, because this environment is not connected to any outside sources or destinations. Use it to see how Amplitude shares and exports data, and how it can connect to other systems.

1.On the Executive summary dashboard, click Subscribe. This window shows how a dashboard is sent on a schedule: the Email tab takes subscribers and a schedule (for example every Monday at 10AM, with or without a CSV), and the Slack and Teams tabs send it to a channel. Look, then close the window without clicking Add.CPUC-19CPWF-06

2.Admins can see every scheduled report, who receives it, and how often at Settings > Organization Settings > Content Management > Subscriptions. You may not have access to this page.CPUC-19

3.Click Data in the left sidebar. Sources are only available inside a project, not a portfolio, so open the project dropdown at the top of the Data menu and choose Toolbox. Click Catalog: the Sources tab lists the SDKs and integrations Amplitude can ingest data from (Web & Desktop, Mobile, Server, and more), and the Destinations tab lists where data can be sent, grouped by category such as CRM, Reverse ETL, and Storage.CPUC-20CPUC-24CPWF-06

4.Read the Export API documentation to see how raw events can be exported, including the sample_rate field that shows how each event was sampled. You do not need to call the API.CPUC-20CPWF-14

5.Select Create > Chart, open the Segmentation tab, and add the events Task Card Created (A) and Document Opened (B). Under Measured as, click Formula, enter UNIQUES(A)/UNIQUES(B), and click Apply Formula to build a custom KPI. Save it as [Initials] - Task card to document ratio.CPUC-20CPWF-14

6.Open any cohort and click Target Users. The window shows where a cohort can be used (a chart, an experiment, a feature flag, a guide, or a survey) and where it can be synced (User Profile API, or Add or Manage Destinations for tools such as a webhook). Click Cancel; do not set up a sync.CPUC-24CPWF-06

7.Power BI, Databricks, Salesforce, and support tools are not set up in the sandbox. The two reference sections below explain how each one connects, how Power BI activity can be brought into Amplitude, and where to find the documentation.CPUC-19CPUC-24CPWF-06

What you should see

How dashboards reach people on a schedule, the export routes Amplitude offers, the sampling field in raw events, and the paths to Power BI, Salesforce, and support tools.

Scenario 8 reference: how other systems connect

These systems are not set up in the sandbox. Here is how each one connects with Amplitude, with links to the documentation.

SystemHow it connectsAmplitude documentation
Power BI

No built-in integration. Recommended: Amplitude to Snowflake to Power BI. Export or stream Amplitude data to Snowflake, then connect Power BI to Snowflake. It supports scheduled refreshes, SQL transformations, and Power BI's native Snowflake connection.

Alternatives: Amplitude to Amazon S3 to Power BI, for larger or recurring exports. Or the Export API into a scheduled pipeline that loads Power BI or a database. The Export API does not support cross-project views, so run it on each underlying project.

  • Snowflake destination
  • Amazon S3 destination
  • Export API
  • Data export options
DatabricksBuilt-in warehouse destination (listed as Early Access in the documentation, and shown as Requested in the sandbox): Data > Destinations > Add Destination > Databricks. Exports events on a schedule you set, with an optional event filter.
  • Databricks destination
SalesforceMarketing Cloud: built-in cohort sync (open a cohort, click Target Users, and add the destination). Sales Cloud and Service Cloud: no built-in destination appears in Amplitude's destination documentation. Use the Cohort Webhook, or send data to your warehouse and sync it with your own pipeline.
  • Salesforce Marketing Cloud V2
  • Cohort Webhooks
ServiceNow and other support toolsThe Cohort Webhook sends cohort updates to the tool's endpoint, with a payload you shape using a FreeMarker template.
  • Cohort Webhooks
AI assistantsAmplitude's MCP server lets an AI assistant ask Amplitude questions. It acts with the signed-in user's own permissions.
  • Connect Amplitude MCP

Scenario 8 reference: bringing Power BI data into Amplitude

Boeing may also want Power BI activity inside Amplitude, for example reports viewed or exports completed. Amplitude has no built-in Power BI source, so the data travels through a small pipeline that you build.

The flow

Power BI activity source to middleware or scheduled job to Amplitude ingestion API

  1. Choose the activity. Decide which Power BI activity matters, such as report viewed, dashboard opened, or export completed. Confirm that Power BI's APIs expose it, or add your own instrumentation to the application that embeds the reports. Also confirm that your organization's privacy policy allows sending it to Amplitude.
  2. Shape each record as an event. A middleware service or scheduled job pulls the activity and maps each record to an Amplitude event: an event_type such as Report Viewed, a user_id (at least 5 characters), a time in milliseconds since epoch, and event_properties such as the report name. Add an insert_id so a retry never creates duplicates.
  3. Send the events to Amplitude. Choose a route from the table below.
  4. Check that they arrived. Open Events & Users > Live Events to watch them come in, then chart them like any other event.
RouteUse it whenWhat to knowDocumentation
HTTP V2 APIYou want near-real-time events at lower volume.Send a POST to https://api2.amplitude.com/2/httpapi (EU projects use api.eu.amplitude.com) with the project API key and an events array. Each request can hold up to 2,000 events and must stay under 1 MB.HTTP V2 API
Batch Event Upload APIYou load on a schedule or in bulk, for example a nightly job or a backfill.Built for scheduled or bulk uploads. The documentation covers its request format and limits.Batch Event Upload API
Event-ingestion integrationYou want a reusable, connector-like solution instead of a one-off job.Build a reusable event-ingestion integration. The documentation covers how to create, test, and submit one.Create an event-ingestion integration
Not the webhook

Amplitude webhooks send Amplitude notifications and cohorts outward. They do not bring data in, so they are the wrong tool for this job.

More: Get data into Amplitude

Wrap up

Pull it together

Can you see all of your work in one place?

Where to start

Click Create in the left sidebar and choose Dashboard.

1.Click Create in the left sidebar and choose Dashboard. Amplitude opens a new dashboard that asks What story should your dashboard tell?

2.Under Or start with, click Existing content. In the Add charts and cohorts panel, search for your initials or filter the Space to your own Space, and select every chart and cohort you saved.

3.Arrange the charts if you like, name the dashboard [Initials] - Bake Off dashboard, and save it to your [Initials] - Bake Off folder. Your Space now holds your folder, your charts and cohorts, and the dashboard that brings them together.

What you should see

A dashboard named with your initials that shows the charts and cohorts you saved, stored in your folder.

Optional bonus

Ask the Global Agent to do it for you

Can the Global Agent do the manual work, explain why, and recommend what to do next?

Where to start

Click Chat & Agents in the left sidebar, then New Chat. Use the Boeing Portfolio View unless a prompt says to select a specific project.

Each prompt below does the same work as the manual scenarios earlier in this guide, but in one request. Every prompt asks the agent to explain why something happened and to recommend next steps, so you get an interpretation as well as a chart. Paste a prompt into the chat, read the answer, then try a follow-up such as go deeper on the top operator or turn that into a notebook. Where a prompt shows [Initials], replace it with your own initials before you send it. The agent's answers will vary from run to run, and the data is synthetic, so results may look unusual.

How to write your own prompt

  1. State your role and goal.
  2. Ask one clear business question.
  3. Give the scope: project, date range, and segments (for example Portfolio View, last 30 days, by company_code).
  4. Chain the steps in order (then...).
  5. Ask it to explain why and to recommend next steps ranked by impact.
  6. Add guardrails (draft only, don't activate) and a format (lead with the answer, then the evidence, and link every chart).

Useful phrases

  • Lead with the answer in two sentences, then show the evidence.
  • Explain why, not just what, and tell me how confident you are.
  • Recommend next steps ranked by impact and effort.
  • Link every chart and cohort you used.
  • Draft only. Don't activate, publish, or connect anything.

A weak prompt and a strong one

WeakShow me errors by operator.
StrongI'm a product lead at Boeing Digital. Which operators are hit hardest by Error Occurred over the last 14 days, and why? Break it down by error_type and product, explain what's driving the top operator, and recommend 3 next steps with the evidence for each.

The prompts

1.Operator workflow friction. Project: Boeing Digital Portfolio View. Paste this prompt into the chat:CPUC-01CPUC-02CPUC-03CPWF-01CPWF-03

I'm a product lead for Boeing Digital. In the Portfolio View, where do users drop off between Event Detail Viewed, Alert Status Changed, and Task Card Created over the last 30 days, by company_code? Explain why the worst-converting operator lags behind the others by comparing converters and drop-offs on every available property. Save the drop-offs as a cohort called "[Initials] - Alert triage drop-offs", show the most common paths ending in Task Card Created, and pull a few rage-click replays. Finish with 3 recommended next steps, ranked by impact.

You should see a funnel by operator, a saved drop-off cohort, the paths leading to Task Card Created, links to replays, and an explanation of what differs for the weakest operator, followed by ranked recommendations.

2.Feature adoption and retention. Project: Toolbox. Paste this prompt into the chat:CPUC-04CPUC-05CPUC-13CPWF-02

In Toolbox, is Fault Finder worth investing in? Compare 90-day retention of users who adopted it in the last 30 days against active users who didn't. Explain why the gap exists and how much of it might be selection bias rather than the feature itself. Break the non-adopters down by user_role and company_code, and recommend which group to target first and how. Save both cohorts with my initials.

You should see adopter and non-adopter cohorts, a retention comparison, a note on correlation versus causation, a breakdown of non-adopters, and a recommended target group.

3.Error root cause. Project: Boeing Digital Portfolio View. Paste this prompt into the chat:CPUC-23CPUC-08CPUC-09CPUC-10CPWF-08CPWF-09

Across the Portfolio View, what caused the recent spike in Error Occurred? Find the biggest anomaly in the last 30 days, explain why it happened by testing error_type, operator, product, and platform, and say how confident you are. Show who was affected and give me a replay. Then recommend next steps, including how we'd catch this earlier. Describe the alert you'd set up, but don't save it.

You should see the largest anomaly, a ranked explanation with a confidence statement, the affected users, a replay link, recommended next steps, and a described (not saved) alert.

4.Operator account review. Project: Boeing Digital Portfolio View. Paste this prompt into the chat:CPUC-07CPWF-07

Prepare an account review for operator TRA. Compare TRA to the other operators over the last 60 days on active users, Task Card Created, Fault Finder Used, and Error Occurred. Explain why TRA is trending the way it is, and what it should do differently. Identify TRA users whose activity dropped and save them as a cohort. Put it in a notebook titled "[Initials] - TRA account review" with charts, a summary a customer success manager could read in 2 minutes, and 3 recommended next steps.

You should see an operator comparison, an explanation of TRA's trend, a cohort of TRA users whose activity dropped, and a notebook with charts and recommendations.

5.Search-to-action effectiveness. Project: Toolbox. Paste this prompt into the chat:CPUC-01CPUC-25CPWF-01CPWF-12

In Toolbox, how well does search lead to action? Build the funnel Search Submitted → Document Opened → Task Card Created for the last 30 days. Explain why users drop off at the weakest step, and show what users who succeed do differently from those who don't, including their paths. Recommend 3 improvements to search, and design an A/B test for the highest-impact one: hypothesis, primary and guardrail metrics, and rough duration. Draft only; don't start anything.

You should see a funnel, a comparison of successful and unsuccessful users, three recommendations, and an experiment design written out but not started.

6.Health scoring. Project: Boeing Digital Portfolio View. Paste this prompt into the chat:CPUC-21CPWF-13

Explain how the Operator health score on the Operator health dashboard is built from its signals. Which operator looks healthiest and which looks most at risk, and why? Build a variant, saved as "[Initials] - Health score (test)", that weights errors more heavily. Tell me which operators change rank and what that says about the model's sensitivity. Recommend how Boeing should choose the final weights.

You should see an explanation of the formula, the healthiest and most at-risk operators, a saved variant with a heavier error weight, and a note on which operators change rank. The original chart must not be overwritten.

7.Targeting and rollout planning. Project: Toolbox. Paste this prompt into the chat:CPUC-11CPUC-13CPUC-15CPUC-26CPWF-04CPWF-12

Plan a staged rollout of a new Quick Bookmarks feature in Toolbox. Recommend which users to start with, using engagement, user_role, and company_code. Build that cohort, explain why it's the safest and most informative starting group, size it against active users, and show how they behave today on Task Card Created. Draft a flag at a 10% rollout for them, leave it inactive, and write guide copy introducing the feature. Recommend what to measure in week 1 and what would make us stop.

You should see a saved cohort with its size, a rationale, a draft flag that is not active, draft guide copy, and week-1 success and stop criteria. The flag must stay inactive and nothing is published. The agent drafts guide wording only; the guide builder itself is used in the UI (see Scenario 5).

8.Proactive monitoring. Project: Boeing Digital Portfolio View. Paste this prompt into the chat:CPUC-23CPUC-08CPWF-08

Set up monitoring for operator health. Create a draft custom agent called "[Initials] - Operator watch" that runs every Monday at 9am. It should compare each operator's active users, errors, and task card creation to its trailing 4 weeks, explain what moved and why, and recommend one action per flagged operator. Don't connect Slack or Teams. Then tell me what the first report would likely flag, based on current data.

You should see a draft custom agent (not active, no destination connected) and a preview of what its first report would flag.

9.Cross-product identity. Project: Boeing Digital Portfolio View. Paste this prompt into the chat:CPUC-14CPWF-05

Do users move between Airplane Health Management, Toolbox, and Asset Lifecycle Planning? Look at users active in more than one product in the last 30 days. Explain what they have in common, whether they're more engaged than single-product users, and which journeys connect the products. Recommend how Boeing should use this for cross-product adoption. Show one anonymized example user's activity across products.

You should see the share of multi-product users, what sets them apart, the journeys linking products, and one example user's cross-product activity.

10.Executive briefing. Project: Boeing Digital Portfolio View. Under the chat box, choose Deep research before sending. Paste this prompt into the chat:CPUC-23CPUC-06CPWF-08

Give me an executive briefing on the Boeing Digital portfolio for the last 30 days. What are the three most important things changing across products and operators, and why? Test the main hypotheses before presenting them, and note any you couldn't confirm. Recommend the top 3 actions for the next 30 days with the supporting charts, written for a VP who has 3 minutes.

You should see three prioritized findings with tested explanations, any unconfirmed hypotheses noted, and three recommended actions with supporting charts.

11.Custom agents. Click Custom Agents in the panel on the left, then New Agent. Browse the templates: Dashboard Agent, Session Replay Agent, Release Impact Monitor, Activation Funnel Watch, Data Assistant Agent, Feature Adoption Tracker, Experiment Readout, and At-Risk Account Radar, or describe what you want in your own words. A custom agent runs on a schedule and sends what it finds. Close the window unless you want to try one; if you do, name it [Initials] - ... and do not connect Slack or Teams.CPUC-23

What you should see

Ten answers from the Global Agent, each with an explanation and ranked next steps, and a look at the custom agent templates. Anything it saves should sit in your own Space and folder.

Good to know

The Global Agent can create cohorts, charts, journeys, notebooks, dashboards, draft flags, and draft custom agents. It cannot publish guides or surveys, pick on-page elements for a Pin step, or activate flags and experiments. Those stay in the interface, as in the earlier scenarios.

Charts the agent builds are drafts until saved. If a prompt asks it to save something, check that it landed in your own Space and folder, and move it if not.

Use your initials in every name. Anything you save here can be added to your [Initials] - Bake Off dashboard from Pull it together.

Prepared for Boeing Digital Services. Sandbox data is synthetic.
